observed_title: On the Bloch and Qp–Carleson measure problems

read_ranges.scope: 逐页阅读全文及参考文献，PDF p.1–30 / paper.md L1–1548；证明链、附录（若有）均纳入阅读。

topic_relevance.legacy-iterated-compensating-measure: direct for the fixed-disk Bloch–Carleson embedding/capacity equivalence; only a methodological analogy for a tree packing constant, not a central-cube theorem.

definitions.name: Admissible dyadic resolution
definitions.statement: A nested sequence of finite measurable partitions of D whose conditional expectations converge in L1, with an ordering fixed at each level.

definitions.name: Packet matrix
definitions.statement: Γ_{μ,N}(R1,R2)=∫Φ_{R1}Φ_{R2}dμ is PSD since it is the Gram form of packet functions.

definitions.name: Bloch capacity
definitions.statement: B_R(μ)=sup_N inf{Σλ_R: λ_R≥0, Γ_{μ,N}≤diag(λ_R)}; C_R is the coefficient supremum over dyadic simple functions.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 / Theorem 1.4: embedding-capacity equivalence
assumptions: μ is a finite positive Borel measure on the unit disk D; R is an admissible dyadic resolution with finite partitions, nesting, L1 convergence of conditional expectations, and fixed ordering.
The function space is the little Bloch space seminorm embedding into L2(μ); the full Bloch norm adds μ(D).
theorem_cards.statement: The seminorm embedding is bounded iff the dyadic packet quantity C_R(μ) is finite, and iff the PSD packet matrices admit finite diagonal domination capacity B_R(μ). The optimal embedding constant is comparable to C_R(μ) and, up to the absolute Grothendieck/duality factor, B_R(μ), for every admissible R.
proof_steps: For sufficiency in Theorem 3.1, approximate ψ∈L∞ by dyadic conditional expectations E_Nψ; the finite coefficient test controls P0(E_Nψ), pointwise convergence follows because K0(z,·) is bounded for fixed z, and Fatou passes the L2(μ) bound.
For necessity, test the embedding on P0(Σ_R c_R1_R), |c_R|≤1, using boundedness of P0:L∞→Bloch; this yields C_R≤best embedding constant.
For C_R≤B_R, any diagonal majorant diag(λ)≥Γ bounds every coefficient quadratic form by Σλ_R.
For B_R≤C_R, write the finite-dimensional SDP dual over PSD X with diagonal X(R,R)≤1; strict primal feasibility gives strong duality.
Factor X as a Gram matrix of vectors of norm ≤1, apply the complex Grothendieck inequality, then Cauchy–Schwarz for the PSD form Γ to bound the dual objective by a universal multiple of C_R.
The full Bloch norm conclusion splits f=f(0)+(f−f(0)), adding μ(D).
gaps: The proof invokes P0:L∞ onto the Bloch space via cited [5, Theorem 3], finite-dimensional SDP duality, and the complex Grothendieck inequality; these are not re-proven here.
The comparison constant is absolute and independent of the chosen admissible resolution in the theorem statement; it depends on those external classical results.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1.7: compactness iff vanishing tail capacity
assumptions: Same finite positive measure and Bloch embedding setting; Sρ={z:|z|>ρ}.
theorem_cards.statement: Compactness of the little Bloch seminorm embedding into L2(μ) is equivalent to boundedness together with B_R(1_{Sρ}μ)→0 as ρ→1 for every admissible dyadic resolution; the statement can equivalently be expressed using C_R.
proof_steps: Compactness implies boundedness and uniform vanishing of the embedding norm on the tails; Theorem 3.1 converts that norm to C_R and Theorem 4.1 to B_R.

Conversely, compact-open convergence of bounded Bloch sequences controls an interior compact disk, while vanishing tail capacity controls the outer annulus uniformly; combine to get L2(μ)-convergence of a subsequence.
gaps: The Qp compactness analogue later in the article is described as a parallel proof; this card concerns the Bloch theorem whose proof is provided.

constant_dependence.explicit: B_R≃C_R≃ optimal seminorm embedding constant with absolute comparison factors; full Bloch embedding includes additive μ(D).

endpoint_limits.measure: The criterion is for finite positive Borel measures on the disk and a specified admissible dyadic resolution. It is not stated for arbitrary trees or L1 weak-type estimates.
endpoint_limits.compactness: Tail capacity must vanish as ρ→1; boundedness alone does not imply compactness.

reusable_methods.method: Linearize the embedding through L∞ dyadic simple functions and a packet Gram matrix
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires a linear projection representation into a Hilbert L2(μ) target; the PSD form does not directly give the user’s L1 weak-(1,1) tree bound.

reusable_methods.method: Replace coefficient testing by diagonal domination via SDP duality
reusable_methods.transfer: Finite dimensionality, PSD matrix, strong duality/strict feasibility, and Grothendieck are essential inputs.

reusable_methods.method: Encode compactness by vanishing tail capacity
reusable_methods.transfer: Transfer requires an established capacity equivalence and a compatible exhaustion of the target domain.
